class.name: FellowTraversalPose3D
class.brief_description: FellowEngine: a character's pose while its [FellowTraversal3D] mantles or vaults — procedural (two-bone IK for the hands and feet, the hips lowered, the torso leaned) or the clip set for the kind.
class.description: A modifier of the character's [Skeleton3D] (after the animation's: an [AnimationTree] or [AnimationPlayer] plays under it). It finds its [FellowTraversal3D] among the children of the skeleton's ancestors (or at [member traversal_path]) and, while a mantle moves the body, poses the bones over whatever the animation plays: the torso tipped towards the wall (the spine and chest), the hips lowered as far as the traversal allows until the shoulders are within the arms' reach of the edge (hanging, pushing up), the hands on the edge (two-bone IK, the elbows out and down), the feet against the wall's face and stepping onto the top, or tucked over a vault (two-bone IK, the knees towards the wall, the feet keeping their turn in the world). When the traversal has a clip for the kind, the clip is played across the mantle instead, its root bone's motion since the clip's start taken out. Blended in and out over [member blend_time]. The targets are placed relative to the skeleton where it is drawn: with physics interpolation on ([member ProjectSettings.physics/common/physics_interpolation]), between two physics ticks (its interpolated transform). The bones are found by their names in common rigs: Godot's humanoid profile ([code]Hips[/code], [code]Spine[/code], [code]Chest[/code], [code]LeftUpperArm[/code], [code]LeftLowerArm[/code], [code]LeftHand[/code], [code]LeftUpperLeg[/code], [code]LeftLowerLeg[/code], [code]LeftFoot[/code] and the right side's), Mixamo's ([code]mixamorig:LeftArm[/code], [code]LeftForeArm[/code], [code]LeftUpLeg[/code], [code]LeftLeg[/code]…), Unreal's mannequin ([code]pelvis[/code], [code]spine_01[/code], [code]upperarm_l[/code], [code]lowerarm_l[/code], [code]hand_l[/code], [code]thigh_l[/code], [code]calf_l[/code], [code]foot_l[/code]…) and Blender's ([code]upper_arm.L[/code], [code]forearm.L[/code], [code]thigh.L[/code], [code]shin.L[/code]…); [member bone_names] names others. See [code]docs/decisions/0180-traversal-mantling.md[/code]. Milestone 201 (decision 0343): while the hands reach for a hold from the air ([method FellowTraversal3D.aim_jump_at_hold]) the hips' spring ([member body_sway]) is off (the body flying is the controller's) and the grip's shape ([member ledge_grip]) comes in at once; until 0.4 s after the hold is caught, a foot the animation puts into the stone under it (a step up the wall) is put on its face instead — the ankle 10 cm off it, the knee 8 cm — the leg's own plane kept.

method.name: get_hang_fit_offset
method.description: How far [member hang_fit] moved the body in the last pose, in world space (metres).

method.name: get_hips_drop
method.description: How far the last pose lowered the hips, in meters.

method.name: get_role_bone
method.description: The skeleton's bone found for [param role], or -1.

method.name: get_sway
method.description: The [member body_sway] spring's offset of the hips in the last pose, in world space (metres).

method.name: get_weight
method.description: The blend of the traversal's pose over the animation's, 0 to 1.

members.member: The seconds the pose takes to blend in when a mantle starts and out when it ends (a clip's last pose is held while it fades).

The body's weight while the pose is procedural (hanging, moving from hold to hold, climbing): the hips hang on a damped spring behind where the traversal shows the body and keep this share of its speed when it changes — caught at the end of a leap they swing on and back, they lag a start — pulled back at [member sway_frequency], damped by [member sway_damping], never further than [member sway_max]; the torso leans back against the swing (with [member lean]), the hands and feet stay on their targets, and the hips go no lower than the arms reach. [code]0[/code]: off (milestone 153, decision 0290).

Bones named for roles, over the names found by themselves: a role's name ([code]"hips"[/code], [code]"spine"[/code], [code]"chest"[/code], [code]"left_upper_arm"[/code], [code]"left_lower_arm"[/code], [code]"left_hand"[/code], [code]"right_upper_arm"[/code], …, [code]"left_upper_leg"[/code], [code]"left_lower_leg"[/code], [code]"left_foot"[/code], [code]"right_upper_leg"[/code], …) to the bone's name.

Seconds over which a clip the traversal plays (a mantle) fades in from the pose this node gave the frame before — the hands and feet on the holds by IK, hanging braced — instead of taking over at once (eased). [code]0[/code]: at once (the braced legs had snapped to the clip's first pose, 74 degrees in a frame). See [code]docs/decisions/0296-the-reference-mannequin.md[/code].

Milestone 203 (decision 0345): [member hang_fit] moves the body no faster than this (m/s), its speed changing by no more than 8 m/s² — a hand taking a hold far above had yanked the body up to it in a tenth of a second (6 m/s, 15 body weights). [code]0[/code]: as fast as it eases (0.1 s).
The feet placed on the wall's face and the top.

Hanging and moving from hold to hold: a hand off its hold (the traversal's grip on it 0) is reached for its target by this share of the IK, the grip eased in and out over a tenth of a second — below [code]1[/code] the animation's own arm (a motion-captured move's) carries the hand through the move and the IK pulls it onto the hold as it takes it — from milestone 198 (decision 0340) homing in over the second half of the hand's way, on the hold as the move catches it, and full again when the pose comes in afresh. [code]1[/code]: the IK's arc throughout, as before (milestone 196, decision 0338).
The hands placed on the edge (and the hips lowered for them to reach it).

Hanging from one ledge (not between holds): each hand's target slid along the edge by this share of the way to where the animation's hand is — its height and depth the edge's —, so a shimmy's hands step as its clip's do rather than as the traversal's stepping (a motion-captured shimmy at the body's pace leaves its hands where it took hold). [code]0[/code]: the traversal's targets (milestone 196, decision 0338).

Hanging or moving from hold to hold, the body moved — up to 0.75 m, eased over 0.1 s — until the shoulders are within the arms' reach of the holds the hands grip (the traversal's [code]hand_grips[/code]): the hands on the stone whatever the clip's pose and the capsule's place, and a hand that takes a hold pulls the body up to it. A hand moving to its next hold reaches for it as far as the arm goes. A clip played from a hang (a mantle) starts where the fitted body was, the move eased out. Milestone 200 (decision 0342): with [member ledge_grip], the fit's own steady drift (up to 1.2 m/s) followed at once, only its jumps eased — the arms no longer short of the holds as the body settles into a hang. [code]false[/code]: the body where the clip and the capsule put it (milestone 153, decision 0291).
The torso tipped towards the wall.

Milestone 198 (decision 0340): hanging, each hand held on its ledge as a climber's by this much: the middle finger's knuckle over the edge, the palm down the face from it (70 degrees from level; flatter where the stone just under the edge stands out, so the palm goes over it; turned towards the shoulder as far as the arm needs to reach), the fingers over the edge onto the top and the thumb by the index finger — once the knuckles are over the top; below it (the arm not yet up to the hold) the fingers open up the face. A step just under the edge (its top no more than 4 cm under it, at least 6 cm out) is held by its own edge. The wrist's place follows the hand's whole way between holds (out of the stone), its shape is turned to over the last 65 % of the way and let go of as it leaves, the wrist's bend held against the forearm as it eases into the animation's. With it the hands' targets are eased over at most 15 ms, the hands come in twice as fast as the rest of the pose (a hold caught from the air) and the elbows' bend turns at most 720 degrees a second. Needs the hand bones' finger children (thumb, index, middle, ring and little or pinky) and the traversal's holds ([method FellowTraversal3D.get_pose_targets]'s [code]hold_left[/code], [code]hold_lip_left[/code] ...). Milestone 200 (decision 0342): a hand on its hold keeps its fingers over the edge wherever its knuckles are (they open up the face only while it is on its way). [code]0[/code]: the hands as the IK leaves them (the wrist on the top 6 cm in over the edge).

The time constant, in seconds, with which the hands' and feet's targets and weights follow the traversal's (no jump where they change: a move's end, a hang's start). [code]0[/code]: off, the targets as given (milestone 153, decision 0290).

While this node poses the body: no bone turned faster than this (degrees a second) from the pose this node gave the frame before — where the traversal's hints, a clip's start or an IK solution would turn a joint over in a frame, the turn is spread over the frames it needs. [code]0[/code]: off. See [code]docs/decisions/0296-the-reference-mannequin.md[/code].

How strongly a limb's bend (the elbow's, the knee's way out) follows the clip's own bend against the way this node points it (out to the side, down, back for an elbow; to the wall for a knee): the two directions, across the limb, added with this weight on the clip's. Where the target passes the pole's line the pole's direction across the limb turns over in a frame; the clip's does not. [code]0[/code]: the pole's alone. See [code]docs/decisions/0296-the-reference-mannequin.md[/code].

Past this share of a limb's reach (0.8 to 0.999), its target is eased towards the reach instead of being cut at it: no arm or leg of the pose snaps straight, and one stretched for a target beyond its reach keeps a little bend (milestone 155, decision 0295: a mantle's legs had been straight a quarter of the time). [code]0[/code]: off (the targets reached up to full extension).
The [member body_sway] spring's damping, a share of critical damping (1: no swing past the rest).
The [member body_sway] spring's frequency, in hertz.
The furthest the [member body_sway] spring takes the hips from where the traversal shows the body, in metres.

Milestone 203 (decision 0345): the share of [member body_sway]'s drive that is vertical. A hanging body swings along the wall and out from it as a pendulum, but up and down its arms and legs move it: at [code]1[/code] the hips lagged a leap's push (pinned while the body rose, then snapping up at 17 body weights) and floated up after it at an even speed. [code]0[/code] in the rooftops showcase.
The [FellowTraversal3D] followed; by default the first found among the children of the skeleton's ancestors.

constants.constant: The left hand (its origin, the wrist, is placed).
The left foot (its origin, the ankle, is placed).
